# Decisions — ai-kit-agent-harness
## Dependency-free local runtime Use Python 3.9 standard library, JSON/JSONL storage, and subprocess adapters.

## LLM-first control boundary Models generate/revise plans, infer dependencies, choose implementation strategy, and synthesize evidence. The harness validates, authorizes, persists, schedules, limits retries, and records events.
## Safe provider defaults Provider calls are explicit and never bypass sandbox or permission controls. Planning and review are read-only; implementation gets bounded write access.
## Advisory model routing Codex is the primary agent and Claude is the preferred independent reviewer, but `.ai-kit/models.yaml` is explicitly advisory until an external orchestrator consumes it.

## Canonical skills with generated projections Use `.ai-kit/skills/` as the editable workflow source and generate byte-identical `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` projections. Generated copies are preferred over symlinks for predictable Windows/WSL behavior.
# Decisions — ai-kit-codex-claude

## Honest enforcement boundary Generic Git hygiene and configured CI tests are mechanical. Planning, acceptance interpretation, independent review, and destructive-operation authorization remain task-aware workflow or host-control responsibilities.

## 2026-08-22 Main index remains user-owned - Decision: staging is permitted only in the disposable worktree to capture new files; promotion applies without `--index` and leaves main changes unstaged. - Because: enabling controlled task execution does not authorize staging or commit.

# Decisions — controlled-orchestrator-v2
## D1 — Contract registry is optional Legacy plans remain valid. Multi-service enforcement activates when `services` or `contracts` is present, avoiding a breaking migration for small repositories.

items.topic: D2 — Contract source approval is explicit
items.summary: ## D2 — Contract source approval is explicit A reviewed implementation task does not automatically approve a public contract. A human-named `approve-contract` transition hashes the current source and changes it to approved.
## D3 — One task, one service Backend, frontend, and database tasks select one registered service. Cross-service behavior is decomposed into per-service tasks plus QA/integration or release tasks.

items.topic: D4 — Hierarchy is metadata, not a global lock

items.topic: 2026-08-22 Git QA is local and baseline remains user-owned
items.summary: ## 2026-08-22 Git QA is local and baseline remains user-owned - Decision: when Git exists, normal install delegates `setup --init` to Git QA and configures only local hooks; it never stages or commits, and `--no-git` opts out. - Because: local Git QA is useful by default, while history creation requires user review and explicit authority.

## 2026-08-22 Preflight and no force-overwrite mode - Decision: existing managed files must be byte-identical; conflicts and symlinks stop the install before any managed file is written, with no `--force` escape. - Because: agent rules, hooks, and CI are security-sensitive project-owned inputs. - Instead of: last-writer-wins copies or heuristic text merging.

## 2026-08-22 Self-contained copied-kit bootstrap - Decision: the executable, manifest, templates, and documentation all live below `.ai-kit/install/`, so copying `.ai-kit/` carries everything needed to bootstrap a root. - Because: portability must not depend on a root file that does not yet exist. - Instead of: a root-level setup script or a network downloader.

# Architecture — canonical-state-convergence

## Consumers and ownership | Consumer | Classification | Target behavior | |---|---|---| | `dag.py` | migrate | consume normalized state; retain DAG/conflict rules | | `orchestrate.py` | migrate | canonical mutations remain harness-owned; legacy Markdown mutation is temporary compatibility | | `worker_manifest.py` | migrate | resolve declared scope through normalized tasks | | `consistency.py` | m

## Decision `state.json` is the only mutable execution authority for a harness-managed feature. `tasks.md` is a deterministic projection when canonical state exists and a read-only compatibility source only when canonical state is absent.

## Failure and recovery - Malformed canonical JSON, feature mismatch, duplicate task IDs, invalid dependency values, and path escape fail closed with stable diagnostics. - Missing/stale projection errors name the repair action. - Repair writes projections atomically without altering canonical state or the event sequence. - Legacy parse errors stay explicit; no heuristic recovery or implicit canoni

## Mutation rules - Harness/coordinator is the sole canonical state writer. - The resolver is read-only and never creates, repairs, or upgrades state. - Legacy Markdown transitions remain available only when `state.json` is absent. - A canonical feature with stale projection cannot be scheduled through legacy scripts; `harness repair` regenerates projections from unchanged state.

## Normalized model Each task exposes `id`, `title`, `status`, `owner`, `scope`, `needs`, `files`, `attempts`, and `instance`. Canonical states map to `todo`, `in-progress`, and `done` for script compatibility while retaining `canonical_status`.

## Resolution boundary `.ai-kit/scripts/task_state.py` owns feature/task state resolution for repository scripts. It exposes a Python API and a bounded JSON CLI. The result always includes `feature`, normalized `tasks`, `source` (`state.json` or `tasks.md`), `canonical`, `projection_matches`, and deterministic diagnostics. Resolution order: 1. Validate the feature identifier and contain all paths

## Rollout and rollback Consumers migrate behind source detection, preserving canonical and legacy readability. Rollback reverts consumer integrations; rollout never rewrites state data. Historical legacy features are not automatically migrated.

# Architecture — controlled-orchestrator-v2 status: approved-for-implementation updated: 2026-08-22
## Components and ownership

## Context The v0.13 engine invokes an implementation provider in the main repository and detects scope violations after the process returns. It can restore harness control files, but an out-of-scope application mutation remains in the user's tree. v0.14 moves the mutation boundary into a disposable Git worktree and makes promotion a separate, post-review control-plane transition.

## Failure modes - No baseline commit or dirty main tree: block before provider call with setup guidance; do not create a commit. - Provider/scope/verification failure: main remains unchanged; record failure and discard only the owned worktree. - Review revise/block: never promote; retain finding evidence and discard owned workspace when the task returns to retry/escalated state. - Main drift befo

### `GitWorkspaceManager` — `.ai-kit/harness/worktrees.py` Owns Git discovery, baseline validation, worktree creation, patch capture, promotion preflight/application, and cleanup. It accepts only an AI-Kit root and explicit feature/task/run identifiers. It never plans tasks, invokes models, changes canonical state, stages the main index, commits, pushes, or merges.

### `GitWorkspaceManager` — `.ai-kit/harness/worktrees.py` Owns Git discovery, baseline validation, worktree creation, patch capture, promotion preflight/application, and cleanup. It accepts only an AI-Kit root and explicit feature/task/run identifiers. It never plans tasks, invokes models, changes canonical state, stages the main index, commits, pushes, or merges.

## Non-functional requirements - Python 3.9 standard library only; Git CLI is the optional runtime dependency. - All subprocess calls use argument vectors, `shell=False`, bounded output, and repository/workspace-specific cwd. - Deterministic errors are testable without Codex or Claude. - No secrets, patch bytes, or raw provider/verifier output enter canonical state.

### Provider request working directory — `.ai-kit/harness/providers.py` `ProviderRequest.working_directory` is an optional internal execution boundary. Subprocess adapters validate it as a real, non-symlinked directory before spawn. Codex uses it for both process cwd and `--cd`; Claude uses it for cwd. Omission retains the provider's configured repository root for planning and compatibility.

### Provider request working directory — `.ai-kit/harness/providers.py` `ProviderRequest.working_directory` is an optional internal execution boundary. Subprocess adapters validate it as a real, non-symlinked directory before spawn. Codex uses it for both process cwd and `--cd`; Claude uses it for cwd.
